properties.name: MEASURED 2026-09-28: the only tool that says which design a server holds (design_identity) is marked as a write, so checking a folder's pointer costs one logged write per session start on flo2.io
properties.statement:
Found while building the first slice of the pointer file. The client checks that the server at `.reflow2.toml`'s address holds the design the file names. Searched for a read-only way to learn a server's graph id: reflow2's handshake (get_info) names no design, and among the tools only design_identity returns `graph_id` directly (tools/skills_tools.rs). It is `read_only_hint = false` because passing `label` renames the design, and flo2.io's gateway treats a call it cannot see is read-only as a write: it ensures the caller is a Contributor and records the call in its write log. So each session started in a folder with a pointer to flo2.io leaves one design_identity entry in flo2's write log.
Not harmful, and the check is worth it (it is what stops a session being attached to the wrong design). The clean fix is a read-only way to ask: the design's id in the handshake, or a read-only identity tool. Either needs a reflow2 release and, on flo2.io, the new tool admitted by its gateway.
